findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the interior baffles of the ice machine to be soiled with black microbial growth. The PIC was informed and plans to hire a professional to clean the interior of the machine. A follow-up will be conducted on September 4, 2026 to ensure the ice machine is clean to sight and touch. 

Inspector also observed the nozzles of the soda machine at the server station to be soiled with black debris. The PIC stated the Pepsi advised against using sanitizer or soaking the nozzles overnight. Education was conducted regarding the requirement for all food-contact surfaces to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized routinely. The nozzles were replaced during the inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed the crock-pot on the cookline was not hot holding cooked chicken at 135F or above. The following internal temperatures were recorded: 105F, 104F, and 108F. The chicken was voluntary discarded during the inspection. An employee turned up the crock-pot and put water and broth inside to test its functionality. After about 10 minutes the crock-pot had an ambient air temperature of 168F. The PIC was instructed to closely monitor the temperature of the crock-pot. Ensure that foods are always hot held at 135F or above.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed that the inside of the ice machine above the outside of the baffles is soiled with debris (near the hinge; not in contact with the ice). The inspector suggests draining the ice to clean inside. Ensure that the inside of the ice machine is clean to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed that the floors of the walk-in freezer were soiled with food spills and debris. An employee cleaned the floors to sight and touch during the inspection. Ensure that the walk-in freezer floors are cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of debris and other soils.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed that the dump sink is not sealed to the wall. All surfaces that are not easily movable must be sealed to the wall (ex. caulking). Ensure that the dump sink is sealed to the wall to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
Seals of the pizza cooler are held on by duct tape. Repair/replace seals so that they meet manufacturer’s specification to ensure that the cold holding unit functions properly. 

4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. (C) Cutting or piercing parts of can opens shall be kept sharp to minimize metal fragmentation.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

The dish machine has a chlorine contact concentration of 0ppm at time of inspection. The sanitizer had run out in the bucket attached to the dish machine. A new bucket was added to the machine but the machine is still testing at 0ppm of chlorine using the proper test strips provided by the company that provides the machine chemicals. A follow up inspection will be conducted to ensure dish machine compliance on 7/21/23.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The soda gun is observed to be soiled. The soda gun was cleaned and sanitized. Clean the soda gun more frequently to preclude the build up of soil form the food surface of the dispenser.  Violation corrected on site.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
Repeat violation from the last routine inspection.
3-501.15: (A) Cooling shall be accomplished with time and temperature criteria by using following methods: FOOD in shallow pans, Separating FOOD into small portions, using rapid cooling EQUIPMENT, stirring food in container placed in ice bath, containers facilitating heat transfer, adding ice, other effective methods. P (B) When placed in cooling or cold holding EQUIPMENT, FOOD containers shall be: arranged to maximize heat transfer through container walls, loosely covered or uncovered, and during cooling period. C

Observed 4 containers of meat sauce in the walk in cooler still cooling with lids on and placed against the side wall of the unit. Leave containers of cooling food uncovered or loosely covered so that air can move around the containers and heat can transfer out of the food being cooled. The sauce containers were 67F, 48F and 53F. According to the kitchen staff the sauce had been cooling for 3 hours. Ice wands were added to the buckets of sauce and lids removed. Provide more effective, monitored cooling process by the next routine inspection. Sauce should be stirred and overseen until the temperature reaches 41F or below throughout the product as the depth of the sauce is greater than 4 inches.

Develop proper  cooling habits for the facility.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. (C) Cutting or piercing parts of can opens shall be kept sharp to minimize metal fragmentation. 

The left door of the small cooler holding lasagna orders and ingredients is not in good repair and does not shut well. Repair door so that it shuts well and keeps cold air in the unit. Repair the door.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
3-501.15: (A) Cooling shall be accomplished with time and temperature criteria by using following methods: FOOD in shallow pans, Separating FOOD into small portions, using rapid cooling EQUIPMENT, stirring food in container placed in ice bath, containers facilitating heat transfer, adding ice, other effective methods. P (B) When placed in cooling or cold holding EQUIPMENT, FOOD containers shall be: arranged to maximize heat transfer through container walls, loosely covered or uncovered, and during cooling period. C

Observed 4 containers of meat sauce in the walk in cooler still cooling with lids on and placed against the side wall of the unit. Leave containers of cooling food uncovered or loosely covered so that air can move around the containers and heat can transfer out of the food being cooled. The sauce was moved to the walk in freezer, ice wands were added and lids removed. Provide more effective, monitored cooling process by the next routine inspection. Sauce should be stirred and overseen until the temperature reaches 41F or below throughout the product. After further discussion, the containers of sauce were moved to the walk in freezer.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor. 

Observed boxes of food, ice cream and ravioli, on the floor in the walk in freezer. The foods were moved up onto shelves.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time. 

Observed sliced ham and sliced roast beef within a bottom reach-in prep cooler to have date mark of 8/24/22. Time exceeds 7 day date marking system. Discussed with multiple employees. Discussed with PIC. Ensure coolers are routinely checked for items that have exceed 7 day date marking system. Items were voluntarily discarded. COS.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

Observed some food/drink splash and debris under the bar area. Observed the spray nozzle at the dish machine area to have some food build-up/debris on the squeezer. Clean non-food contact areas routinely to hinder debris build-up. Discussed with PIC.

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.comment:
3-801.11: (D) FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact READY-TO-EAT FOOD as specified under ¶¶ 3-301.11(B) and (E). 

Observed the ice scoops to be within the ice at both the bar and server station ice basins. Discussed with PIC. Handles of the ice scoops should be placed upright in the ice to avoid cross contamination with ready-to-eat foods (ice). COS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Observed the soda nozzle at the bar to have mold within the nozzle. Discussed routine cleaning of food-contact surfaces with PIC. PIC had employee remove the soda nozzle to clean - wash, rinse, sanitize. COS.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

(REPEAT) Observed caulking at the dish machine area to be half completed. PIC/employee’s were not aware Inspector wanted both the area before the dish machine and the area of the 3 compartment sink to be caulked to the wall. Caulk is missing. Caulk all equipment that is attached to the wall. Discussed repairs with PIC. Ensure caulking before next routine inspection. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspections on 6/8/21 and 11/10/21.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water. 

Observed white fish and salmon to be thawed within sealed ROP. Directions on packaging of individual fish state to remove and thaw outside packaging. Ensure proper thawing method (see above). Best practice to remove fish from packaging before thawing. Discussed with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

(REPEAT) Observed caulking to be missing around the dish area and 3 compartment sink area. No caulk between walls and dish machine/3 compartment sink. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 6/8/21.

Kitchen hand sink next to this area is missing caulking, as well. Ensure caulking before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).  

Observed salad dressing bottles within the salad basin of the top salad prep cooler. Cease practice. Keep salad dressing out of the loose leaf lettuce and within the bottom of the prep cooler. COS. 

Observed chopped chicken in a bowl within the hot holding crock pot resting on top of the hot held chicken. Cease practice. Do not place bowls on RTE food items like hot held chicken. COS.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned. 

Observed knife store in between prep coolers. Cease practice. Knife is a food-contact surface and should be prevented from cross contamination. Keep knives in clean areas. COS.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-101.19: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. 

Observed chest freezer in kitchen to have accumulation of frost. De-frost the chest freezer to hinder frost accumulation. Clean before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

Observed caulking to be missing around the dish area and 3 compartment sink area. No caulk between walls and dish machine/3 compartment sink. Caulk before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11  (P)  Ready-to-eat (RTE) foods stored below raw proteins. Store RTE foods above raw proteins so they are separate and protected from cross-contamination. Reference 3-302.11.

Observed several large containers of parmesan cheese within walk-in cooler to be stored below raw proteins (steaks, sausage) that were in lidded containers. Discussed storing RTE cheese above the raw proteins with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114  (P) Quaternary ammonium sanitizer measured 100 ppm at sanitization buckets within kitchen. Maintain concentration at 200 ppm to 400 ppm as indicated on manufacturer's label. Reference 4-501.114.

Observed both sanization buckets within the kitchen to have low quaternary ammonium - 100 ppm each. Discussed routine changing of sanitization with PIC. Corrected - buckets were remade and tested at 300 ppm. COS.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Utensil holder and can opener food contact surface is soiled with dust, dirt, food residue and other debris. Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).

Observed utensil holder container to be soiled with debris at bottom. Food contact utensils (spoons, spatulas, etc.) are in contact with bottom of container. Observed can opener to have a small accumulation of debris. Discussed routine cleaning of food contact surfaces with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17  (Pf) Date marking is not on multiple foods throughout facility. Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41 deg F or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date). Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

Observed multiple items throughout facility to lack date marking:
1. Walk-in cooler: milk, orange juice, pasta.
2. Bottom reach-in coolers: ravioli, rigatoni pasta, sauce in shallow metal tray, sour cream, cottage cheese.

Discussed date marking with PIC. Facility actively date marks majority of items throughout facility. Ensure all items are date marked and discarded within 7 days. This is a repeat violation since the last original inspection on 9/10/19. COS.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.12  (C) In-Use Utensils are stored incorrectly. Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F. Reference 3-304.12.

Observed several in-use utensils to be storaged incorrectly:
1. Scoops of parmesan cheese within walk-in cooler were not stored in a manner that allowed the handle to be above the top of the food. Corrected scoops and discussed with PIC. COS. 
2. Knife at prep counter was stored beneath the cutting board. Discussed knife storage with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11  (C) Tile coving in the toxic substance storage area was found in a state of disrepair, or not to be smooth and easily cleanable. Except as specified in Section 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are smooth and easily cleanable.  Reference 6-201.11.

Observed facility to have a broken tile and coving coming from wall in the toxic substance storage area. Discussed repairs with PIC.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 (A & B) (C) Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. Except for cleaning up a spill or other accident, cleaning should be done during periods when the least amount of food is exposed such as after closing.  Reference 6-501.12 (A & B).

Observed build-up on soda debris near soda lines in back toxic substance storage area. Splatter was observed on walls and tile floors. Discussed routine cleaning with PIC.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed red sauce and meat in the prep cooler without dates. CORRECTED- PIC labeled foods with the dates they were prepared/opened.
3-501.17 (A) Refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or Discarded when held at a temperature of 5ºC (41ºF) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. (Pf)

Observed ham in prep cooler dated 8/28. CORRECTED- Ham was discarded.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18 (A) A FOOD specified in ¶ 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in ¶ 3-501.17(A). (P)

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment: Frozen fish is thawing while still wrapped in reduced oxygen packaging (ROP). Packaging must be removed from fish in ROP prior to thawing under refrigeration or running water.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13 (E) REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGED FISH that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment (1) Prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in ¶(A) of this section; or (2) Prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in ¶ (B) of this section. (C)

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Raw shell eggs and raw shrimp noted stored above container of ready-to-eat butter packets in the 2 door make table cooler near the bar pass thru window. Items were rearranged at the time of inspection with raw items stored on the bottom shelf.

-> Please store raw food items by cooking temperature and below ready to eat foods to prevent possible contamination. Reference 3-302.11.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
Fish such as salmon and cod, which are received frozen, were found thawing while in ROP vacuumed sealed packaging on the speed rack in the walk-in cooler and in the 2 door undercounter cooler across from the deep fryers at the time of inspection. Discussed scoring the packaging to allow air into the packaging. 

->Frozen fish is thawing while still wrapped in reduced oxygen packaging (ROP). Packaging must be removed from fish in ROP prior to thawing under refrigeration or running water. Reference 3-501.13.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
Wet wiping clothes noted on preparation tables in the kitchen area. Discussed keeping wiping cloths in sanitizer solution with proper concentrations. 

->Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animal foods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
The following containers were noted in disrepair and missing pieces of plastic:
Blue lidded container in the bottom area of the salad make table cooler
Lid of container used for breading in the 2 door make table near the bar pass thru window
Lid of container used for ravolis in the make table cooler across from the deep fryer

->In-use equipment and/or utensils in disrepair. Remove from use and replace with equipment that is durable and easily cleanable meeting National Sanitation Foundation/ANSI standards. Reference 4-201.11.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.comment:
Observed four containers of sauce that was 70F and cooled from last night. All containers were discarded during the inspection. Facility has 6 hours to cool -- 135 F-70F in two hours and 70-41 F in an additional four hours.
750-140(b)  Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 135°F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F or below within 4 hours.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed ice paddles on the floor in the walk in freezer. Make sure ice paddles are at least 6" off the floor.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed the soda nozzle in the bar area to be soiled. Clean the food contact surface.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed the drain underneath the handwashing sink in the server station to be soiled. Clean the drain.
750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Observed red meat sauce with no time marked. When cooling foods make sure to time mark potentially hazardous foods.
750-140b Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed bruschetta past the seven days. The bruschetta was discarded during the inspection. Make sure to date mark potentially hazardous foods and use or discard foods within seven days.
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
1) Observed duct tape on the plastic piping underneath the bar plumbing sinks. 2) Observed a missing vacuum breaker cap at the dish machine near the spray hose. Make surfaces smooth and easily cleanable.
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
1) Observed the soda nozzle at the bar to have some soil accumulation. 2) Observed the can opener blade soiled. Clean the food contact surfaces as needed.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment:
Observed forks and knives stored with food contact surface up being ready to be rolled. Store in a manner to prevent potential cross contamination.
750-850 Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination.  Spoons, knives and forks shall be touched only by their handles.  Cups glasses, bowls, plates and similar items shall be handled without contact with inside surfaces or with surfaces that contact the user’s mouth.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Observed a very small section in the dish area to have some mold. Clean the walls as needed.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Toxic items properly stored
findings.comment:
Observed the tonic water stored underneath the chemicals. The tonic water was moved during the inspection.
750-1310 All toxic items must be properly stored (i.e. segregated from food) to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all chemicals.

findings.title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
findings.comment:
Observed chicken improperly thawing. Make sure to properly thaw chicken.
750-240 Potentially hazardous foods shall be properly thawed by one of the  following method. 1. Under refrigeration 41°F or below, 2. Under  potable running water 70°F or below or below with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose food particles into the over-flow, 3. In microwave as part of the cooking process, 4. As part of the cooking process.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
Observed wet wiping cloths stored on countertops. Make sure to store wet wiping cloths in the sanitizer solution.
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
Observed no paper towels at the handwashing sink in the kitchen. Paper towels were provided during the inspection.
750-1120e A supply of soap and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.comment:
Observed a coat stored with cleaning chemicals. Coats and personal belongings must be stored separate from food.
750-1280 Adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from the food preparation and food storage area to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all employee belongings.

findings.title: Toxic items properly stored
findings.comment:
Observed tonic water stored underneath cleaning chemicals. The tonic water was moved to a higher shelf during the inspection. Chemicals must be stored separately from food.
750-1310 All toxic items must be properly stored (i.e. segregated from food) to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all chemicals.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.comment:
Observed the mop stored improperly. The mop was inverted during the inspection.
750-1390 Maintenance and cleaning tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners and similar equipment shall be maintained and stored in a way that does not contaminate food.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: The blade of the can opener is observed to be soiled. 750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use. The opener was cleaned immediately.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: The drain under the sink at the wait area is soiled. 750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris. Clean and maintian clean.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment: Ice wands observed on the floor of the walk in freezer under bottom shelf. 750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination. The wands were removed and sanitized. Store ice wands above serface of floor as to not contaminate them.

findings.title: Foods handled with minimal manual contact
findings.comment: Upon arrival individuals were observed to handle ready to eat cheese and bread with bare hands. 750-280 Food handlers shall avoid direct hand contact with ready to eat foods.  When handling ready to eat foods use suitable utensils (gloves, tongs, scoop, deli tissue, etc.) Properly protect ready to eat foods. Hands were washed and gloved utilized.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment: Drawers holding utensils under the prep table near dish have dust and crumbs in the bottom. 750-860 Cleaned and sanitized utensils an equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means. Clean drawers and maintain free of accumulated soil.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment: Upon arrival observed ice scoop at wait station to be in ice with handle touching the ice. 750-290 Ice scoop shall be stored on a clean surface or in the ice with the handle extended out of the ice. Scoop was removed to clean dry surface.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: Cabinet area under the wait station hand sink is soiled with water and the pipes under the hand sink are also soiled. 750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris. Clean and maintain clean.

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.comment: Italian beef and Italian sausages observed on the hot holding table at 125F. 750-150(b)  Hot potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at 135°F or above except during the cooling process. Store hot foods at 135°F or above. (Except for rare roast beef which may be held at 130F.) Foods were placed into pots and heated to 165F before being placed back onto the hot holding table. The water in the area under these items was not very deep and was not even touching the bottoms of the pans. More water was also added to the pans for hot holding.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.comment: Four large batch containers of meat sauce are observed to be in the corner of the walk in cooler at between 63F and 71F. They had a date of 4-21 on them. Also, there was no time for cooling written on them.  750-140(b)  Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 140°F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F or below within 4 hours. The batches are in white bulk containers of about 20 gallons each. The sauce was denatured with chlorine and the  staff will work on discarding it down the garbage disposal.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
The walk in the basement has pans catching water drips. It is evident that one of the pans has overflowed and some water has been on the shelf above plastic containers holding bags labeled "sauce" which appear to be seasoning mix. The container is large and sticks out past the edge of the shelf and is not covered. 
750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food. Protect this food from potential contamination by placing a lid on the container, fixing the walk in, or moving the spice mix.

findings.title: Foods handled with minimal manual contact
findings.comment: Observed employee making plates to sprinkle parsley on the food with bare hands and move noodles on the plates with bare hands. 750-280 Food handlers & consumers shall avoid direct hand contact with ready to eat foods.  When handling ready to eat foods use suitable utensils (gloves, tongs, scoop, deli tissue, etc.) Do not handle ready to eat foods with bare hands.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: The soda gun at the bar is soiled with mold. 750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use. Wash, rinse, and sanitize regularly to avoid accumulation of mold on the food contact surface.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment: The pipe on the sump pump is disconnected and some water is observed on the floor and lid of the sump pit. The drain lines of the walk in the basement are dripping, 750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code. Repair the above listed plumbing and drain line issues.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: Floor at the bar is soiled especially in area under and behind equipment.  750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors and maintain clean.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: Pipes under sink at wait station are soiled, 750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris. Clean and maintain clean.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment: Unwrapped straws for drinking are stored on the bar unprotected. 750-880 Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user. Protect straws properly.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: Floors were being swept with a broom while sauce is being prepared and tubs of sauce are open in the area. 750-1220 Cleaning of floors shall be done during periods when the least account of food is exposed.  Lids were placed on the sauce tubs so that the floors could be cleaned in a way that takes into account food safety.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: 750-140(b)  Observed baking sheets of cooled noodles cooked today to not have the time indicated on the label. Discussed with cook and time was indicated during the inspection. Racks of these trays were observed in the walk-in cooler already temping at under 40F for the dozen or so that were probed. Noodles cooked about thirty minutes prior to temping were probed and already temping at 55-61F. Facility boiled the noodles and then cools them under cold water. Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 140°F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F or below within 4 hours.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.comment: 750-1390 Wet mops were observed stored on the floor next to the mop sink. Stored in the available hanging storage unit during the inspection. Maintenance and cleaning tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners and similiar equipment shall be maintained and stored in a way that does not contaminate food.
